cases.name: sample_jni_onload
cases.comment: OLLVM-flattened JNI_OnLoad: a state variable (var_178) is threaded through if-chains and a table load (g_1e14d0 base + state*8) that picks the next block. No 'rounds' key, so it runs at the harness default of 8 -- pinned, which makes it a wall rather than a budget, so a regression in rounds-per-level fails the case instead of quietly costing time. It needed 24 before Phase A2 and takes 8 now (7 rounds of discovery, one to confirm the fixpoint): carrying a branch's candidate set with its discovery lets the round that lifts a level also open it. fold-resolved-branch (Phase A1) turned every single-target resolved branch into a plain fallthrough, which is most of why gotos/ifs are this low; the remaining ones are the genuine 3-way switch, its own back edge, and one dead-end self-loop the obfuscator pads with. The 13 remaining ternaries are the ones Phase A4 deliberately left: a select nested inside an address computation or hoisted to a shared temporary is not a statement, and rewriting it as one would invent control flow the code does not have.

cases.name: sample_mega_dispatcher
cases.comment: The same obfuscator turned up to a size nothing resolves whole: 320 blocks behind one entry, and ~300 of its computed branches are 'ldr xT,[x26,xI,lsl#3]; br xT' where x26 never narrows to one value, so the table shape never matches and the value set stays top. The driver still reaches a real fixpoint in 4 rounds -- this is not a round-budget case -- and until Phase A3 the run then failed the Resolved gate and produced nothing at all for 320 understood blocks. --allow-unresolved seals each unanswerable branch as an opaque terminator naming the expression it could not evaluate, so the case now scores what was recovered and tracks the holes as a number. Lowering max_unresolved_branches is the measure of progress on data-dependent brind resolution; raising it is a regression.
